items.explanation: The 1904 Corollary declared the U.S. an 'international police power' that could intervene in Latin America to keep Europeans out, prop up order, and remove unfriendly regimes — all three purposes at once.
options: A. Keeping European powers out of the Western Hemisphere
B. 'Assisting' Latin states in economic or political crisis
C. Removing hostile governments in the hemisphere
items.stem: The Roosevelt Corollary to the Monroe Doctrine was intended

option_explanations.A: Keeping European powers out of the Western Hemisphere was the original Monroe Doctrine (1823) and part of the Corollary, but the Corollary went further — it claimed an American right to intervene directly. This alone understates what the Corollary was intended to do.
option_explanations.B: 'Assisting' Latin states in crisis — collecting debts, restoring order — was exactly the policing power Roosevelt claimed in 1904, but it was only one piece of the Corollary's purpose.
option_explanations.C: Removing hostile governments was indeed part of how the Corollary was applied, but again only one piece. The Corollary claimed all of these purposes at once.
option_explanations.D: Correct. The 1904 Roosevelt Corollary declared the United States an 'international police power' in the Western Hemisphere — empowered to keep Europeans out, intervene in Latin states' crises to preserve order, and remove unfriendly regimes. All three purposes were claimed together.

items.explanation: Spain's reconcentration camps in Cuba — herding civilians into disease-ridden camps to starve the insurgency — horrified American humanitarians and fed war fever in 1898.
options: A. They were horrified by Spain's reconcentration policy in Cuba
B. They ignored the yellow press's editorials
C. They wanted to help Filipino natives
D. They sought American economic interests in Cuba
items.stem: Many American humanitarians first backed the Spanish-American War because

option_explanations.A: Correct. Spain's 'reconcentration' policy — forcing Cuban civilians into disease-ridden camps to starve the insurgency — was widely reported in the American press, and the suffering it caused turned humanitarians toward war against Spain in 1898.
option_explanations.B: The opposite of what happened. The yellow press's lurid editorials about Cuban suffering fed the war fever; humanitarians absorbed that coverage rather than ignoring it.
option_explanations.C: American humanitarians in 1898 were focused on Cuba, not the Philippines. The war began over Cuba; the Philippine annexation debate — and the humanitarian outcry over subjugating Filipinos — came after the war.
option_explanations.D: Economic interests in Cuba motivated business-minded expansionists, not humanitarians. The humanitarians' argument was about Cuban suffering under Spain, not about sugar profits.

items.explanation: Missionaries saw empire as a God-given field for evangelism — converting the 'heathens' of Cuba, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines.
options: A. They hoped to restrain other imperialists' zeal
B. They admired the spirituality of native peoples
C. European church leaders endorsed imperialism
D. They saw empire as a chance to convert new peoples
items.stem: American missionary leaders supported imperialism because

option_explanations.A: Missionaries did not oppose imperialism to restrain other imperialists — they actively supported American expansion because it opened new fields for their work.
option_explanations.B: Missionaries did not admire native spirituality; their purpose was to replace it. They supported imperialism as an evangelical opportunity, not out of respect for indigenous religions.
option_explanations.C: European church leaders' views were not the reason American missionaries backed imperialism. Their motivation was their own: empire meant new peoples to convert.
option_explanations.D: Correct. American missionary leaders supported imperialism because they saw empire as a God-given field for evangelism — a chance to convert the 'heathens' of newly acquired Cuba, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines.
